title: The precepts of the Church (CCC 2041–2043)
hookLine: Sunday Mass, yearly confession, Easter communion, fasting, support

lines: WHAT'S THE LEAST I HAVE TO DO?
cards: Folding chairs, a box of donuts, a whiteboard marker running dry: a confirmation class in a church basement.
A fifteen-year-old in the back raises his hand with a question others may be wondering too: okay, but what's the least I have to do to still count?
The catechist laughs, and then, instead of dodging, she writes a short list on the board. Five lines. Today's word is that list, and the surprising way the Church itself describes it.

teach.b: In your first weeks you met Sunday, the obligation nobody explains as a gift. Here is the whole list it belongs to. The Catechism calls them the precepts of the Church, five of them.
First: attend Mass on Sundays and holy days of obligation, and rest from work that gets in the way of keeping the day holy. Second: confess your sins at least once a year.

Third: receive Communion at least during the Easter season. Fourth: keep the days of fasting and abstinence the Church sets. Fifth: help provide for the needs of the Church, each according to their ability.
The Catechism doesn't present the precepts as the goal of the Christian life.

It calls them positive laws meant to guarantee a very necessary minimum: the least a Catholic owes in prayer and moral effort, so that love of God and neighbor has room to grow. A floor, not a ceiling.

Think of them as the bones of a year: every week a Sunday; every year a confession and an Easter Communion; fasting days, when what the body wants comes second for a while; and the collection basket, or time and skills given instead, so the parish lights stay on and the poor are fed.
Each one ties a private life to the life of the whole Church.

So the honest answer to what's the least I have to do is this list. And the honest follow-up is that the least is only where it starts. Nobody falls in love and asks how few dinners they can get away with.

how: Catholics are taught the five precepts in catechism classes; parishes post the holy days and the fasting days each year, and the precepts tie a Catholic's year to Sunday, Lent and Easter.

games.q: you're the catechist. a teenager asks: what's the least I have to do to still count? what do you say?
o: dodge the question; it's the wrong attitude.
give him the five precepts, and say they're a floor, not a ceiling.
tell him there are no rules at all.
games.why: the Catechism itself gives the list and calls it a very necessary minimum: where the Christian life starts, not where it ends.

practice: Go through the five slowly, one line at a time: Sunday, confession, Easter Communion, fasting days, supporting the community.

For each, notice where you are with it right now, without scolding yourself; if you're not Catholic, ask what your own small minimum is, the few things you keep no matter what. If you pray, ask for help with the one that's hardest.

wordCard.voice: Precepts. The five basic duties the Church asks of every Catholic: Sunday Mass, yearly confession, Easter Communion, fasting, and support for the Church. Today's word.

orig.note: Latin: commands, rules; plural of praeceptum.

carryVoice: Your line: the minimum, not the maximum. The floor is there so love has room to grow. Rest well.
